title: Flood Insurance and Your Mortgage in Myrtle Beach, SC
description: When a lender requires flood insurance in Myrtle Beach, how much coverage you need, how the premium affects approval, and how a house leaves the flood zone.
h1: Do You Need Flood Insurance to Get a Mortgage in Myrtle Beach?

faq.q: Is flood insurance required for a mortgage in Zone X?
faq.a: No. A lender requires flood insurance only when the house is in a Special Flood Hazard Area, a FEMA zone starting with A or V, or in a Coastal Barrier Resources System area. In Zone X you may still buy flood insurance by choice.

faq.q: How much flood insurance does my lender require?
faq.a: Fannie Mae requires the lowest of three amounts: the cost to rebuild the house, the NFIP maximum of $250,000 for a single-family building, or the loan amount.

faq.q: Can I use private flood insurance instead of FEMA's NFIP?
faq.a: Yes. Regulated lenders must accept a private policy that meets the federal definition of private flood insurance, and Fannie Mae accepts a private policy with coverage and terms at least equal to an NFIP policy.

faq.q: Is there a waiting period for flood insurance when I buy a house?
faq.a: No. An NFIP policy bought in connection with a new loan takes effect at closing if the application and premium are submitted by then. Other new NFIP policies normally wait 30 days.

faq.q: Does flood insurance have to be paid through escrow?
faq.a: Usually. Federally regulated lenders must escrow flood insurance premiums on home loans, with limited exceptions. The premium is then paid from your monthly mortgage payment.

faq.q: How do I get a house removed from a flood zone?
faq.a: The owner applies to FEMA for a Letter of Map Amendment, with elevation data such as a surveyor's or engineer's certification. If FEMA issues the letter, the lender no longer requires flood insurance on that house under Fannie Mae's rule.
